The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.75/18 Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi.
2.
Briefly narrated facts of the present case are that the accident in the present case took place on 20.03.2018.

It is the case of the petitioner that on 20.03.2018 at around 9:35 PM, he was riding on his bicycle and when he reached at Pusta Road, Mother Dairy, Kailash Nagar Red Light, PS Gandhi Nagar, Delhi, offending truck bearing registration No. HR-74A-2929, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from the back side and without blowing any horn and applying safety measures, the driver of the offending vehicle hit the petitioner from back side, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Petitioner was admitted in SDN Hospital, Dilshad Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali.

On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 appeared with counsel at the time of filing of DAR.
The respondents no. 1 and 2 who are the driver and owner of the offending truck filed written statement.
Written Statement was also filed by R-3/insurance.

In the written statement filed by R-1 and R-2, it is stated that no accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No.
HR-74A-2929 and they have been falsely implicated in collusion with injured.
Accident was caused because injured was not plying his bicyle properly and lost control.
R-1 had valid DL and offending vehicle was duly insured.

R-3 / insurer has mentioned in its written statement that the DAR is incomplete and the offending truck was dangerously loaded, as per para 66 of DAR, which is violation of permit condition but IO has not provided the photographs of the vehicle and particulars of the goods.
The offending vehicle bears Hayana Registration number but IO has filed RC issued by RTO, Baghpat, U.P.
The site-plan is incomplete and no independent eye witness was examined.
There was contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner for riding his bicycle in the middle of the road.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 20.05.2019 : -
(i) Whether the petitioner Kartik Chand Sharma suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 20.03.2018 at about 9:35 pm at Main Pushta Road, Mother Dairy Kailash Nagar Red Light, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Gandhi Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR74A2929 by respondent no.1?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if yes, at what rate and for which period?(OPP)
(iv) Relief 5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Kartik Chand Sharma has examined himself as PW-1 and exhibited in evidence his medical treatment record and bills, pan card and aadhar card and DAR.
Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir was examined as PW-2 and proved on recorded the disability certificate Ex.PW-2/A and assessment sheet Ex.PW-2/B.
The respondents have not led any evidence.
6. I have heard Ld. counsel for petitioner and considered the written arguments.
Record has been perused.

7. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1 :

Whether the petitioner Kartik Chand Sharma suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 20.03.2018 at about 9:35 pm at Main Pushta Road, Mother Dairy Kailash Nagar Red Light, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Gandhi Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR74A2929 by respondent no.1? (OPP)
8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. Now in this case, the petitioner Kartik Chand Sharma is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.

He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
HR-74A-2929.
He was not cross

- examined by the respondents no.1 and 2 and during cross examination by Ld.counsel for R- 3/Insruance, he denied that the accident occurred as he had jumped red light and came in front of truck which was taking right turn on green light.
He also denied the suggestion that the accident occurred as he was riding on the extreme right lane of the road, which was not designated for bicycles.
10. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1/Mubarik Ali, the driver of the truck.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such a charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.
12. Respondent no.1, the owner/driver of the offending vehicle, did not lead any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
13. It is seen that the driver of the offending vehicle was unknown to the petitioner and there is no reason for false implication.
He was apprehended from the spot itself, as mentioned in the Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and from filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner received injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Mubarik, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

ISSUE No.2:
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

17. Now, in the present case, the injured Kartik Chand Sharma @ Pappu has suffered from degloving injuries in foot region (foot and ankle) and laceration injuries of the size 0.5 cm was seen in left side temporo parietal region and as per the medical records, the opinion on the nature of injuries was given as grievious in nature.

Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows :-

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
18.
Petitioner has proved some of his medical bills.
Under this head, actual medical bills are reimbursed.
The original bills which are on record are of Rs.25,278/- (Ld.
Counsel for petitioner has claimed Rs.24,786/- towards expenditure on treatment but bills and calculation of bills is of Rs.25,278/-).
Therefore, I award Rs.25,278/- as compensation under this head.
PAIN AND SUFFERING:
19 . There is nothing in the testimony or MLC of SDN Hospital or the petitioner (which is part of DAR) to suggest that he remained hospitalized for any given period in the said hospital.

In his testimony, petitioner deposed that he was given first aid at SDN Hospital and thereafter, he was referred to higher centre and taken to GTB Hospital where he was hospitalized for a period of 3-4 days.
In his cross examination, he clarified that he was referred to GTB Hospital at 1:00 am night.

There is no document of GTB Hospital filed on record by petitioner or by IO with DAR to suggest that PW-1 was taken to GTB Hospital on the intervening night of 20.03.2018-21.03.2018 but the treatment papers as exhibited in the evidence as Ex.PW-1/1 by the petitioner reflect that he was treated in the GTB Hospital as an OPD patient from 26.05.2018 to 03.08.2018.
There is no counter suggestion to the petitioner that he did not remain admitted in GTB Hospital for atleast 3 days.
The nature of injury suffered by the petitioner was grievous in nature.
MLC also reflects that the petitioner had degloving injury in foot region and laceration injury was found in temporo parietal region.
The medical documents also show that the petitioner required dressing for injury and patient had reported 'pain while walking', to the doctor, on his visit to doctor on 03.08.2018.
His injuries were follow up case of digloving injury.

Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained,
petitioner must have remained under some pain, discomfort and suffering for atleast 5 months.
Therefore, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.30,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
It is seen that IO has paginated the DAR and mentioned in the Index of DAR, the last document as arrest memo from page 61 to 63.
However, it is seen that some photographs, some pages of inner case diary and photostate copies of some of the ambulance bills are also on judicial record.
There is nothing in the DAR to suggest that these ambulance bills were verified.
Petitioner has not stated anything in his testimony to suggest that he was visiting hospital on amublance over a period of time.
It is admitted by PW1 in his cross-examination that he has not filed original bills of Shri Balaji Ambulance Services.
Hence, the ambulance bills are not proved on record and cannot be taken on its face value.
There is no explanation by the petitioner for non filing of the bills in original and even in the calculation of expenses given by him, he had not referred to these bills.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.15,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and Rs. 5,000/- towards special diet charges.

Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head, it cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
22. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.25,000/- (15,000+5,000+5,000) under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
23. Petitioner has claimed that he was working on handdrill (kharad machine) with Vishwakarma Enterprises, Vishwas Nagar, Delhi and was getting salary of Rs.16,000/- per month plus over time.
He has not placed on record copy of his salary slip or bank statement reflecting his employment and salary.
IO has mentioned monthly income of the injured as Rs.1,500/- in DAR.
However, IO has not placed on record any document in support of this.

No education qualification of petitioner has been divulged by him in his examination-in-chief and in his cross-examination, though he stated that he has studied upto 9 th class, he further stated that he does not have any document in support of his education.
Hence, assertion of PW-1 regarding his educational qualification has to be taken with a pinch of salt.
He admitted the suggestion that M/s. Vishwakarma Enterprises had been sealed in the sealing operation conducted by EDMC.
He was also given suggestion that he was not working as a hand drill operator with M/s. Vishwakarma Enterprises, which was denied by him.
Here, it is relevant to mention that nowhere the date of sealing is mentioned and further no such suggestion was given to PW-1 that he was unemployed on the date of accident.

Hence, considering the testimony of PW-1 and dependence of his family on him solely as claimed by him and not assailed by the respondents, it can be reasonably assumed that he was working, even though it is not established as to where he was working at the time of accident and his income has to be taken as per Minimum Wages Act of unskilled worker applicable in Delhi at the time of accident, as petitioner is a resident of Delhi.

The petitioner has claimed that he was working on handrill with M/s Vishkarmama Enterprises, however, he has not mentioned and proved on record, the exact nature of his work and his competence for the same, so as to deduce that he was a skilled worker.
Further, in the written submission filed by him, he has claimed compensation on the basis of minimum wages of an unskilled worker.
The evidence of the petitioner shows that he remained hospitalized for around 3-4 days.
Petitioner, though did not specify how long he remained on bed, it can be assumed that he may have remained indoors on account of the accident for about 2 months.
It is nowhere mentioned in any of the medical documents that petitioner was advised bed rest for any given period.

However, considering that the petitioner sustained grievious injuries, it is not difficult to presume that in case of degloving injuries, he might have been disabled from work for at least two months as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Therefore, I award Rs.27,168/- (13,584X2) as compensation under this head.

LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO PERMANENT DISABILITY.
24. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.
The disability certificate of Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of disability due to crush injury left foot and ankle (lower limb).

Dr. Sanjeev Gamhir has been examined as PW-2 and deposed that the patient was found to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 13% in relation to left lower limb and the disability had been calculated on the basis of guidelines issued by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He deposed that the range of motion of the patient with regard to hip and knee were normal as the injuires had been sustained in ankle.
The disability has been assessed at 8% with regard to the ankle and 5% with regard to deformity.

He further deposed that the patient can walk independently without support, climb stairs, stand on both legs, stand on affected leg, squat on floor, sit cross leg,
knee, take turns etc.
The petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.
Therefore, he has not proved that due to this injury, his income has reduced.

Further, it is seen that though he claimed to be working on a 'hand drill (Kharad Machine), he himself has admitted that the premises of the claimed employer Vishkarma Enterprises has been sealed and even while stating so, he did not reflect on the date, on which the same was sealed and no document was produced to show that he was acually employed and working with Vishwakarma Enterprises and if so, what was the exact nature of his work.

The employer has not been examined to reflect on or explain the job on the "hand drill" being done by petitioner and if he was so employed, whether he was looking after the hand drill or operating the same.

However, considering the testimony of PW-1 and considering the fact that there is no document to suggest that he is well-educated, it can be safely assumed that petitioner could have been employed as a labour and because he has disability due to degloving injury, it is not difficult to assume that this disability will affect his day-to-day life and profession at least to a minor extent, as labour work may involve standing or squatting for long duration.
Therefore, I presume that the petitioner must have suffered at least 5% functional disability, in carrying on with his profession.
In view of this, I believe that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

On the basis of his income taken as per minimum wages act of unskilled worker (in the calculation sheet filed on record by the petitioner, he has himself claimed compensation on the basis of Minimum Wages of an unskilled worker) as on the date of accident i.e. Rs.13,584/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be Rs.1,63,008/-.
25.

The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner was 28.07.1968,
which would mean that he was 49 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 13 would be applicable. Further, as the petitioner has not led any evidence to suggest that he was not in an permanent job, his income has to be taken as per the fixed salary and hence, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 25% has to be considered, as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 50 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali.

sentences.text: The yearly income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.1,63,008/-.
In this after adding 25% of the future prospects amounting to Rs. 40,752/-, the yearly income with future prospects will become Rs. 2,03,760/-.
In this, yearly income, a multiplier of 13 will make the future income as 2,03,760x13= Rs.26,48,880/-.
5% loss of income due to 5% percent functional disability will mean that the overall loss of income to the petitioner shall be 5% of Rs.26,48,880/- which will be Rs.1,32,444/.

Therefore,
this amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES.
26. Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities.

 ISSUE No. 3:-
Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
Petitioner has pursued his case diligently.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY:
29. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
In the case at hand, R2 is the registered owner of the vehicle, which was insured on the date of offence.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali.

30. During oral arguments, Learned counsel fro R3 submitted that in the DAR, under the column of apparent contributing circumstances, it is mentioned by IO that the vehicle was dangerously loaded and hence it is a case of over loading and permit violation and recovery rights may be given to the insurance company.

Learned counsel for R-1 and R-2 submitted that the submission made by counsel for R-3 lack merit and the respondents were not booked for permit violation by the IO and there is no evidence on record in this regard either.
I have perused the case file which reflects that the connected criminal case is of offence u/s 279/337 IPC and u/s 119 /177 of M.V. Act.
There is nothing brought on record by the insurance company or IO to suggest that the vehicle was over loaded or that there was any permit violation by the offending vehicle.
Hence, there is no merit in the argument made by learned counsel for insurance company seeking recovery rights.

RELIEF:
31.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal, award a total compensation of Rs.2,49,890/- (rupees two lakhs forty nine thousand eight hundred ninety only)
along with interest @ 7.5 % per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no.3 / insurer.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
11. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.
If any party does not accept such a charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.
12. Respondent no.1, the owner/driver of the offending vehicle, did not lead any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.
In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Hence, considering the testimony of PW-1 and dependence of his family on him solely as claimed by him and not assailed by the respondents, it can be reasonably assumed that he was working, even though it is not established as to where he was working at the time of accident and his income has to be taken as per Minimum Wages Act of unskilled worker applicable in Delhi at the time of accident, as petitioner is a resident of Delhi.
In view of this, I believe that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.
On the basis of his income taken as per minimum wages act of unskilled worker (in the calculation sheet filed on record by the petitioner, he has himself claimed compensation on the basis of Minimum Wages of an unskilled worker) as on the date of accident i.e. Rs.13,584/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be Rs.1,63,008/-.

which would mean that he was 49 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 13 would be applicable. Further, as the petitioner has not led any evidence to suggest that he was not in an permanent job, his income has to be taken as per the fixed salary and hence, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 25% has to be considered, as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 50 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali.
